title: Turn a guarded blank with two push tools, centre kept, no hand in the guard
instruction: Keep both grippers outside the grey guard. Use the blue and orange push tools to turn the yellow blank clockwise until its white edge points to the green mark, keeping the blank centred between the four white ticks.
context: A flat workpiece may need reorienting inside a low guarded machine pocket before inspection or the next operation. The opening admits thin tools but not a gripper around the blank (O*NET 51-4041.00, positioning material for machine work). The scene tests remote physical manipulation only; it does not model a running machine or heat.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y left, table top 74.75 cm). Yellow blank 12 x 12 x 2.4 cm, 150 g, friction 0.2, with a white edge strip, centre (30, 0). Blue push tool: 40 mm wide, 20 mm tall flat paddle at (21.1, +3.5) on a 16 cm bar with a 3 x 3 x 13.5 cm handle stem and a balancing tail at y +20.5, 80 g; orange tool mirrored at (38.9, -3.5). Grey guard: four 2 cm posts at (30 +- 12.5, +-12.5) and a rail frame with underside 9.25 cm above the table, clear area 25 x 25 cm. Four white ticks 9.5 cm from the centre on the axes; green angle line at -45 degrees.
scoring: Measured at the end, held 1 s. 0 if the blank tilts over 8 degrees, a blank corner reaches the guard (over 12.5 cm from the centre), its centre is over 8 cm off, or a tool's handle stem is inside the guard footprint. 0.25 if the blank has turned at least 12 degrees clockwise. 0.5 if yaw is -25 degrees or beyond and centre drift at most 45 mm. 0.75 if yaw is -33 to -57 degrees and drift at most 30 mm. 1.0 if yaw is -37 to -53 degrees, drift at most 15 mm, tilt at most 8 degrees and both tool paddles are clear of the blank (centres over 78 mm from its centre along its axes).
reset_notes: Blank at the centre with its white edge facing forward (+x); the two tools 2 cm from the blank's faces, handle stems outside the guard.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; blank and tools are free bodies with no joints, pins or springs; the blank has low table friction (0.2) so a single push slides it. Nothing is code-driven. Scoring uses the blank pose and the two tool poses.
